title: Inscribed Ultimatums and Fates: Trial Count, Boss Keys and Trialmaster Access
summary: An Inscribed Ultimatum opens the Trial of Chaos at the Temple of Chaos. Its Area Level decides the room count (4 / 7 / 10); only the 10-Trial version drops a Fate. Collect Deadly, Victorious and Cowardly Fates from the three Trial bosses, then clear another 10-Trial run and insert all three into the door to fight the Trialmaster.
description: How Inscribed Ultimatums and the three Fates work in Path of Exile 2 0.5: Area Level to Trial count, where each Fate drops, and how to open the Trialmaster's door for your final Ascendancy points.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Inscribed Ultimatum and the three Fates - Deadly, Victorious and Cowardly - the keys that open the Trialmaster's door in the Trial of Chaos

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Take an Inscribed Ultimatum to the Temple of Chaos to start a Trial of Chaos. Its Area Level sets the room count: 39-59 = 4 Trials, 60-74 = 7 Trials, 75-80 = 10 Trials. Only the 10-Trial version drops a Fate. Collect all three Fates - Deadly (Bahlak, the Sky Seer), Victorious (Chetza, the Feathered Plague) and Cowardly (Uxmal, the Beastlord) - then clear another 10-Trial run and insert the three Fates into the door in the final reward room to fight the Trialmaster.
calloutDetail: The area-level thresholds above are the current 0.5 values published on the wiki; confirm them against your own client when 0.5.4 lands, as GGG can shift breakpoints between patches (current 0.5, pending in-game verification).
You do NOT need the three Fates to run a Trial of Chaos for points 1-6; you only need them to spawn and open the Trialmaster door for points 7-8.

answers.label: Use for
text: Entering the Trial of Chaos for Ascendancy points, and (with all three Fates) challenging the Trialmaster for your final two points.

answers.label: Check first
text: Read the Ultimatum's Area Level. If it is below 75 it will only give 4 or 7 Trials and will NOT drop a Fate.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Wasting a high-level Ultimatum by failing the run - failing forfeits the attempt, and you must start a new Ultimatum.

facts.label: What it is
note: An Inscribed Ultimatum plus its three possible Fate keys form the Trial of Chaos access family.

facts.label: Where to use
note: The altar in the Temple of Chaos consumes the Ultimatum to begin a run.

facts.label: Room count
note: Set by the Ultimatum's Area Level: 39-59, 60-74, 75-80.

facts.label: Fate drop
note: Only Area Level 75-80 Ultimatums show a Fate label and drop a Fate from the round-10 boss.

facts.label: Consumed on use
note: The Ultimatum is spent when the Trial starts; Fates are spent when you open the Trialmaster door.

sections.title: The Inscribed Ultimatum family
intro: The Trial of Chaos access family has one entry key (the Inscribed Ultimatum) and three end-game keys (the Fates). You farm the Ultimatum from anywhere in the endgame, and you farm the Fates only from 10-Trial runs. All three Fates are required together to open the Trialmaster's door.

members.title: Inscribed Ultimatum
body: A consumable trial key that drops from monsters across the campaign and endgame (drop level 39). Take it to the Temple of Chaos altar to begin a run of 4, 7 or 10 Trials based on its Area Level.

members.title: Deadly Fate
body: Drops from Bahlak, the Sky Seer, the round-10 boss of a 10-Trial Ultimatum labelled Deadly. One of the three keys needed for the Trialmaster door.

members.title: Victorious Fate
body: Drops from Chetza, the Feathered Plague, the round-10 boss of a 10-Trial Ultimatum labelled Victorious. One of the three keys needed for the Trialmaster door.

members.title: Cowardly Fate
body: Drops from Uxmal, the Beastlord, the round-10 boss of a 10-Trial Ultimatum labelled Cowardly. One of the three keys needed for the Trialmaster door.

properties.label: Item class
notes: Metadata class 'Inscribed Ultimatum'; the Fates share the Trial of Chaos item family.

properties.label: Consumed on use
notes: The Ultimatum is consumed when you start the Trial; each Fate is consumed when you insert it into the Trialmaster door.

properties.label: Tradeable
notes: Both Inscribed Ultimatums and Fates can be traded or bought on the Currency Exchange, so you can also buy a missing Fate instead of farming it.

properties.label: Drop level
notes: Inscribed Ultimatums begin dropping at Area Level 39 and can scale up to Area Level 80.

properties.label: Number of Trials
notes: Decided by the Ultimatum's Area Level: 39-59 gives 4 Trials, 60-74 gives 7, 75-80 gives 10.

properties.label: Fate label
notes: Shown beneath the Trial count ONLY on Area Level 75-80 Ultimatums; it names the round-10 boss and its matching Fate key.

sections.title: How to get Inscribed Ultimatums and Fates
intro: The entry key drops almost anywhere; the Fates are gated behind the highest-tier Ultimatums. There is no deterministic Fate vendor - you either farm 10-Trial runs or trade for the missing one.

routes.label: Monster drops (Ultimatum)
body: Inscribed Ultimatums drop from monsters from Act 3 onward and throughout the endgame, with higher Area Levels appearing in higher-tier content.

routes.label: 10-Trial runs (Fates)
body: Only an Area Level 75-80 Ultimatum runs 10 Trials and fights a Fate boss on round 10. Each run drops ONE random Fate, so you need several runs (or trades) to collect all three.

routes.label: Currency Exchange / trade
body: Because Ultimatums and Fates are tradeable, you can buy a specific missing Fate from other players instead of re-farming the matching boss.

routes.label: Corrupted magic Ultimatums
body: The Trialmaster can drop corrupted magic Inscribed Ultimatums with two affixes (a reward prefix and a dangerous area suffix). These are a higher-risk re-run, not a separate acquisition path.

steps.label: Open the Trial of Chaos
body: Take the Inscribed Ultimatum to the Temple of Chaos and use it at the altar. The Ultimatum is consumed and a run of 4, 7 or 10 Trials begins.

steps.label: Clear to round 10 (for Fates)
body: If your Ultimatum is Area Level 75-80, survive all 10 rounds. The round-10 boss is one of the three Fate bosses and drops a single random Fate.

steps.label: Collect all three Fates
body: Repeat 10-Trial runs (or buy the missing ones) until you hold Deadly, Victorious and Cowardly Fate at the same time.

steps.label: Open the Trialmaster door
body: Clear another 10-Trial Ultimatum while holding all three Fates. A door appears in the final reward room near the Ascension Shrine - insert the three Fates to enter the Trialmaster's Tower.

compare.note: Points 1-6 need only the Ultimatum; points 7-8 need the three Fates and the door.
before: You hold an Inscribed Ultimatum (any level) and run the Trial of Chaos for Ascendancy points 1-6.
after: You hold all three Fates and clear a 10-Trial run, opening the Trialmaster door for points 7-8 and his unique loot.

sections.title: Area Level to Trials matrix
note: The Ultimatum's Area Level is the only thing that decides how many Trials you face and whether a Fate can drop. There is no other way to raise the count.

items.label: Right Area Level for your goal
checks: If you want a Fate or the Trialmaster, confirm the Ultimatum is Area Level 75-80 before using it.
items.why: Lower-level Ultimatums cannot drop Fates or spawn the door, wasting the run for that goal.
items.fix: Hold low-level Ultimatums for points 1-6; only spend 75+ Ultimatums on Fate farming.

items.label: Hold all three Fates before the door run
checks: Verify Deadly, Victorious and Cowardly Fate are all in your inventory (not just stash) when you start the 10-Trial run that should open the door.
items.why: The door only appears if you complete a 10-Trial run while carrying all three Fates.
items.fix: Run or trade for the missing Fate first; a partial set will not spawn the door.

items.label: Gear for 10 Trials + Trialmaster
checks: Make sure your build can both clear 10 Trials and survive the Trialmaster's opening Sunder if you push for points 7-8.
items.why: The Trialmaster is far tankier than the round bosses and can one-shot an under-prepared character.
items.fix: Cap elemental resistances and build effective HP before attempting the door.

rows.benefit: 4 or 7 Trial Ultimatums grant the first six points
rows.recommendation: Use any Ultimatum you find; no Fates needed

rows.benefit: 10-Trial Ultimatums drop one random Fate each
rows.recommendation: Run 75+ Ultimatums or buy the missing Fates on the exchange

rows.benefit: Final two Ascendancy points and a guaranteed unique drop
rows.recommendation: Only attempt with all three Fates and solid defences

rows.gain: None - the run ends and forfeits accumulated rewards
rows.loss: The Inscribed Ultimatum is consumed with no Fate and no points
rows.recommendation: Only push 10-Trial Fates on a build that can reliably clear the rooms and afflictions.

rows.loss: Compounding debuffs can brick the run before round 10
rows.recommendation: Pick the 'least bad' affliction for your build each room; avoid no-regen and monster-speed stacks.

rows.gain: Final Ascendancy points and unique loot on success
rows.loss: A clipped opening Sunder can delete an under-geared character
rows.recommendation: Cap resistances, build effective HP, and pre-roll the moment the arena loads.

entries.question: Why did my 10-round Trial end with no Trialmaster?
summary: A player finished a 10-Trial run but the Trialmaster door never appeared.
editorialAnalysis: The door only spawns if you complete a 10-Trial run WHILE holding all three Fates. Finishing the run with zero, one or two Fates opens only the normal reward room.
officialAnswer: Collect Deadly, Victorious and Cowardly Fate, then clear another 10-Trial Ultimatum to spawn the door.

entries.question: I have all three Fates - why won't the door open?
summary: Player holds all three Fates but the door does not open after a run.
editorialAnalysis: The Fates must be in your inventory when you START and FINISH the 10-Trial run, and the run must be a 10-Trial (Area Level 75-80) Ultimatum. A 4 or 7 Trial Ultimatum will never spawn the door regardless of Fates held.
officialAnswer: Use an Area Level 75-80 Ultimatum and keep all three Fates in your inventory through the run.

entries.question: My Ultimatum says 'Deadly' - does that mean it drops the Deadly Fate?
summary: Player assumes the label guarantees that specific Fate.
editorialAnalysis: The label names the round-10 boss for that Ultimatum, but which of the three Fates you actually receive is still random per run. The label only tells you which boss you will face, not a guaranteed Fate.
officialAnswer: The label shows the boss; the dropped Fate remains random, so you may still need other runs or trades.

problems.symptom: My Ultimatum only shows 4 or 7 Trials
directAnswer: Its Area Level is below 75. Only Area Level 75-80 Ultimatums run 10 Trials and can drop a Fate or spawn the door.
checks: Hover the Ultimatum and read its Area Level; use a higher-level one for Fate farming.

directAnswer: You did not hold all three Fates during the run. The door requires Deadly + Victorious + Cowardly Fate in inventory at completion.
checks: Confirm all three Fates are in your inventory before starting the next 10-Trial run.

directAnswer: The Fate drop is random; the boss label only names the boss, not a guaranteed Fate. Keep running or buy the missing one on the exchange.
checks: Trade for the specific missing Fate if farming is inefficient for your build.
